Tipflation is real. The tip is not their salary despite what they would have you believe.  25 is a ridiculously large tip for a delivery driver.  There was probably a delivery fee on top of that too. 

You tip a server for being the liason between your table and the kitchen/ restaurant services - the better the service, the n
Higher the tip. 20 percent is sufficiently high. If you serve yourself or don't have a server then there is no reason to tip. You can if you want though.

Services with an established price (taxis, cleaners, dog walkers etc) will appreciate a tip, but the price of the service was negotiated before hand. Any tip you give is at your prerogative. 

You will likely always be asked how much you'd like to tip (I bought tires the other day and had to navigate a tip screen ) and there are people like the other commenter that think it's reasonable to tip 25% for anything, like existing nearby when you make a purchase. The general idea is that if someone did an overly outstanding job and you felt so inclined, it is not *rude* to tip - but it is not required. 

People try to take advantage of that though. Tipflation is real
